summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology with hands-on embedded firmware experience in bare-metal C on ARM Cortex-M4 (STM32), FreeRTOS task coordination, and I2C/SPI/UART peripheral integration. Track record of hardware bring-up, from custom PCB fabrication and schematic capture through chip-level debugging with oscilloscopes and logic analyzers, plus accelerometer and ToF sensor integration across microcontroller and single-board platforms.

Linux Administration: systemd service management (unit files, auto-restart, non-root isolation)

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and AI/ML integration end-to-end.
Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Organized 10+ exhibitions and technical workshops covering Arduino, PCB design, and SolidWorks.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to STM32 over UART.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built a Cortex-M4 temperature monitoring firmware in embedded C with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.
Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at 1 Hz update rate.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Resolved 11 integration failures (servo brown-out, stale-frame capture); achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials).
Integrated dual VL53L0X ToF sensors for contact-aware grasping via TCA9548A I2C mux.
Deployed the Jetson-side arm bridge as a systemd service with auto-restart and static IP networking for multi-device registration.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
